title: A right adjoint of a monomorphism-preserving functor preserves injective objects
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be categories and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be functors with $G$ right adjoint to $F$. Assume that $F$ carries monomorphisms to monomorphisms. Here an object $I$ of a category is \emph{injective} if for every monomorphism $f:X\to Y$ and every morphism $g:X\to I$ there is a morphism $h:Y\to I$ with $h\circ f=g$ (in an abelian category this is injectivity in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]). Then for every injective object $I$ of $\mathcal D$ the object $G(I)$ is an injective object of $\mathcal C$.
